newsitem.title: LEBANON: Solidere leads Beirut stocks upwards.
newsitem.headline: Solidere leads Beirut stocks upwards.

text.p: Solidere A shares rose to their highest level of the year on Thursday on news that the company will open up its shares to ownership by foreigners and local banks and companies.
Other active stocks gained or maintained strength. All three bank shares traded at alltime highs while Solidere B maintained a two-month high.
"It is an excellent day on the bourse," said a broker who asked not to be identified.
The LIBX bank index climbed 0.26 percent to 179.27. The LISPI general index rose 0.56 percent to 93.13 and the BLOM general index increased 2.08 percent to 1039.04.
Total market turnover fell to 349,626 shares from 373,364 for a value of $4,142,740 against $4,586,340.
Solidere A rose to $12 from $11.5 and B was unchanged at $12. The shares traded in heavy demand and brokers said the latest news would further fuel demand.

"Demand on Solidere today was mainly due to the news. The timing of the news was excellent. It stopped some investors from walking out and pushed hesitant investors to bid immediately. It is a reversal of trend," the broker said. "Finally people are waking up to Solidere, realising that the company is undervalued. Solidere is working very professionally and I think it is an excellent value added company," the broker added.

Banque Audi rose to a record $27.625 from $27.5. Demand exceeded supply by more than twofold. A report that Audi had bought medium-sized bank Credit Commerciale du Moyen Orient (CCMO) appeared to come too late to affect the day's trading and an official announcement was still awaited.

"We will see more and more takeovers in the coming period. It is good for the banking sector, giving it more depth in terms of business. Otherwise, bank stocks are in a consolidation mood," the broker said.
Bank of Beirut rose to a new high of $4.5 from $4.43 and 40,000 shares traded on the bourse floor at $4.5. Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce was unchanged at a record $21.
Of the four industrial firms, only Ciment Libanais traded unchanged at $1.2812.
There was no trade in Ciments Blanc, Eternit and Uniceramic.
